sourceNote: The deer mesh (assets/models/deer/deer.glb, assets/models/deer/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the socket to the wrist, a side wall of the trunk under each arm, and arms 1.25 times longer. tools/blender/deer_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. deer.glb stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/deer_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, because the seated bind of the app depends on them.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the skin normals with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). This removes thin dark slits at the back of the arm root.

armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube, as on the fox.
armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments. Each elbow and wrist has a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the rings of its joint in the bind. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings (gap of tools/blender/deer_arms.py).

name: Deer

app.note: The size of the parametric deer, 1.2 times larger: 1.6769 m for each unit, the standing shoulder joints at 0.535 u (0.897 m), and the skull top between the antlers at 1.429 m. The reach is the reach of the arms that are 1.25 times longer.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 does not stretch the arms in the rig. The arms of deer-arms.glb are already 1.25 times longer than the source arms (step_shape() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py, called by tools/blender/deer_arms.py), so that the left forearm stays out of the chest at the harp.
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh, and the chair fits the legs.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the antler tips, +z forward, +x the left side. The elbow, forearm twist, wrist, and paw joints are the joints of the longer arms. source_joints() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py holds the source joints.

studio.bindArmsNote: The bind upper arm points out, forward, and 27 degrees down, nearer to the hanging source arm than the bind of the other meshes. This bind keeps the shoulder ring of the left arm wide and the left socket free of folds in the play.
studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The tail has one bone, so it needs no bind direction.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

weights.rigidPaintedNote: The faces at these points take the mean of the painted weights of their corners, one face after the other. Six faces lie in the crease at the front of the left socket, which folds when the deer plays the harp. The last face lies under the right armpit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips. It starts 0.03 units above the knee and ends 0.03 units above the thigh joint.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only. The ears and the antlers stay on the head, so earBase lies above the head. The tail ball holds the puff tail.

smooth.note: The ten vertices at the back end of the left armpit line move half of the way to the middle of their neighbors in 4 rounds (smooth_box() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). This makes the black notch under the raised arm smaller, with a smoother outline.

pointFlip.note: The edge at this point is the diagonal of one quad of the tube at the front of the right inner elbow (point_flips() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bent elbow of the seated bind makes this diagonal the long one, and its thin face then folds. The other diagonal does not fold.

flip.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh deer --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the other meshes. The eye box holds the left eye of the front view. The nose box holds the dark nose at the front of the muzzle.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.128). The values of front and back are the values of the dog.

crease.note: The values of the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, and the wolf.

sit.note: The values of the dog, with top and carryTail. top 0.1945 puts the flat underside of the haunch on the seat top. With carryTail, the tail ball moves down with the root of the tail, so that the faces under the tail do not stretch into a dark column.
